name: Capri Blue
lede: Capri Blue is a deep greenish blue, named for the water of the island of Capri.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
St Clair glosses Capri blue as a sapphire-like shade, named for the water inside the Blue Grotto (Grotta Azzurra) on the island of Capri [3]. The library records it in Ridgway's atlas of 1912, in RAL 5019 and in ISCC-NBS block 160 [1]. It lies near [[teal]] and [[turquoise]] [1].

The swatch here is the Ridgway match; the RAL paint is a darker, bluer color [1]. Different systems use the one name for different blues, a reminder that place names are loose [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Capri Blue appears in 0.13% of the 23,781 paintings in our archive, as photographed [2]. It is rarer than 67% of the named colors, and it peaks in the 1800s at 0.1% of that century's paintings [2]. Inside a painting it is split between light and shadow roles, 36% each at most [2]. Only 32 paintings hold it, so the numbers are thin [2]. In printed English the word peaks in the 1930s [2].
